_comment: cell_live settings. Every entry has value, unit, source and status (VERIFIED, FROM PHOTO, ASSUMED, CONFIRM, or SETTING for a choice we made). Unknown values are null with status CONFIRM; a value that is deliberately not used is null with status SETTING. Relative paths are relative to the repo root.

move_port.unit: TCP port (never opened by the live checks)

alarm_files_dir.unit: folder with Dobot's alarm_controller.json and alarm_servo.json

connect_timeout_s.unit: s, per socket connect and read

belt_do.unit: digital output index, object belt start and stop: ENA of its TB6600 driver through a series resistor
belt_do.source: photos of the station, 17 Nov: photo 3, notebooks/week-03/Rashmika/Readme.md section 2.6, handwritten DO list (DO3 start and stop); notebooks/week-03/Choton/code/config/settings.json robot.belt_do = 3

belt_on_value.unit: DO3 level that runs the object belt (on a TB6600, current through ENA usually stops the motor, so 0 is expected)
belt_on_value.source: DobotStudio test, Sazzad, 17 Nov 16:29 (0 runs the belt), confirmed by Sazzad 17 Nov: the runs with 1 never stopped the belt (testing/live_runs/20261117_172313.csv)

belt_dir_do.unit: digital output index, object belt direction: DIR of its TB6600 driver through a series resistor
belt_dir_do.source: 17 Nov: handwritten DO list (DO4 direction), photo 3, notebooks/week-03/Rashmika/Readme.md section 2.6

belt_dir_forward_value.unit: DO4 level that moves the objects towards the robot

belt_enable_do.unit: digital output index, object belt enable ('Conveyor enable (Power ON)'); its on level: lab test T5
belt_enable_do.source: 17 Nov: handwritten DO list; wiring confirmed by Rashmika (Choton's handover, 17 Nov)

belt_enable_on_value.unit: DO16 level that lets the object belt run
belt_enable_on_value.source: runs 17 Nov, confirmed by Sazzad: DO3 0 + DO16 0 for 60 s did not move the belt (testing/live_runs/20261117_175839.csv); DO3 0 + DO16 1 ran it (20261117_172313.csv pauses and run ends)

box_belt_do.unit: digital output index that tells the box belt controller to move the closed box on (only for belts.box_restart = dobot_output)
box_belt_do.source: not used (team decision 17 Nov): the box belt runs on its own sensor and an operator takes the closed box

do_bit_order.unit: how feedback digital_outputs bits map to DO channels

feedback_readable_while_held.unit: true/false: can 30004 be read while another program holds 29999/30003

link1_mm.unit: mm, J1 to J2 (two-link model of the M1 Pro for the J1 check, control/arm_reach.py)
link1_mm.source: q_actual from the feedback port, 17 Nov: J1 82.27, J2 -50.87 deg at (197.6, 302.4) and J1 75.32, J2 -61.96 deg at (245.28, 239.67); a 200 + 200 mm two-link arm gives the same angles to 0.01 deg

link2_mm.unit: mm, J2 to the tool axis (two-link model)
link2_mm.source: same q_actual readings as dobot.link1_mm, 17 Nov

arm_side.unit: left (J2 below 0) or right: MovL keeps the arm on this side
arm_side.source: q_actual J2 = -50.87 and -61.96 deg, 17 Nov (feedback port); notebooks/week-03/Choton/code/config/settings.json robot.arm_left_code = 0, SetArmOrientation(0) in every run log

j1_range_deg.unit: deg: the M1 Pro turns J1 from -85 to +85 deg; a straight move that needs more ends in controller alarm 23
j1_range_deg.source: docs/hardware_facts.md, Robot, Spec: joint ranges (vendor spec screenshot, origin/Rashmika-Branch:R2/Images/day2/Image3.jpg); fits 17 Nov: J1 = 82.27 deg at home works, a line that needed 90.1 deg was refused (testing/live_runs/20261117_190902.csv)

reach_limit_mm.source: team message 2026-11-16; Choton_Week3_Notebook.md 14 Nov next steps (lid within about 375 mm)

teacher_approval.source: approved in the lab by Leo, 17 Nov

poll_interval_s.unit: s between dashboard and feedback checks

reach_max_mm.source: team message 2026-11-16; kept at 375 on 17 Nov (decision Sazzad): Choton's handover, lab 17 Nov (new worktable and camera stand, 15_robot_setup.py) says use up to 370 mm, but his taught box drop (369.8, 27.9) is 370.9 mm from the axis; singularity alarm 32 only at 399.8 mm

reach_min_mm.source: Choton's handover, lab 17 Nov (new worktable and camera stand, 15_robot_setup.py): use 175-370 mm from the robot axis

arm_j1_max_deg.unit: deg: an item whose pick point needs a larger |J1| on the arm's side is not picked (out of reach); the belt brings it further
arm_j1_max_deg.source: chosen 17 Nov: the robot holds J1 = 82.27 deg at home (q_actual) and refused a path that needed J1 = 90.1 deg (controller alarm 23, testing/live_runs/20261117_190902.csv), which fits the M1 Pro's J1 range of +/-85 deg (docs/hardware_facts.md, joint ranges, FROM PHOTO); 80 deg keeps 5 deg of margin

speed_percent_max.unit: % (SpeedFactor), highest speed allowed for a run

box_slot_tolerance_mm.unit: mm: the open box's centre (camera) must be at most this far from the taught box slot, or the run pauses before anything is placed
box_slot_tolerance_mm.source: chosen 17 Nov: in testing/live_runs/20261117_193551.csv the box centre was (357.5, -49.1), 78 mm from the box slot (369.8, 27.9), and the card and both candies landed beside the box on the lid; the items fill most of the box, so it must stand close under the slot

lid_min_from_slot_mm.unit: mm: a lid detected nearer than this to the box slot is not picked (it is the filled box, or a lid already on it)
lid_min_from_slot_mm.source: chosen 17 Nov: in testing/live_runs/20261117_195652.csv the filled box was seen as 'lid 0.64' at (358.5, 32.1), 10 mm from the box slot, and the lid step picked from inside the box; a lid lying beside the box (about 120 mm wide, like the box) has its centre more than 100 mm from the slot

lid_grip_offset_max_mm.unit: mm: a lid whose centre is beyond the reach may be gripped this far from its centre, towards the robot, at a point inside the reach, and is put down with the same offset; 0 = off, the lid is then taken at its centre only
lid_grip_offset_max_mm.source: off (0) since 17 Nov: gripping a lid off its centre is a new way for the robot to move, so set it only with the teacher's approval. Why it exists: in testing/live_runs/20261117_195652.csv the lid lay against the box on its upstream side at (351.5, 175.3), 392.8 mm from the robot, 17.8 mm beyond the reach (375 mm), and could not be taken; the lid measures about 120 x 155 mm in the camera picture, so 20 mm off its centre is still well inside it (a value of 30 covers that case)

box_wait_timeout_s.unit: s waiting for an open box standing still

object_feed_timeout_s.unit: s the object belt may run without the full set

belt_settle_s.unit: s after the object belt stops, before the pictures

box_still_frames.unit: frames the open box must stand still

box_still_px.unit: px a box may move between frames and still count as standing still

objects_ready_frames.unit: frames in a row the full set must be seen

pick_area_mm.unit: robot mm [x min, x max, y min, y max]: only a card or candy whose centre is inside this area of the object belt is counted and picked; null = only Choton's area (his calibration marks + 20 mm) applies
pick_area_mm.source: the pick area as it was on 17 Nov: Choton's rule (yolo_lib._belt_zone, calibration marks + 20 mm) on notebooks/week-03/Choton/code/config/homography.json of 2026-11-17_14-30-00 (marks from x 176.08 to 254.43 and y -74.88 to 163.63 mm). Fixed here so that a new calibration with marks on both belts does not widen it to the box belt, where the filled box is seen as a candy or a card

feed_stop_y_mm.unit: robot y in mm: the object belt also stops when an object the box still needs is at this y or lower (the objects move towards lower y), so it stays in the pick area; null = only the full set stops the belt
feed_stop_y_mm.source: chosen 17 Nov from measured values: Choton's pick area ends at y = -94.9 mm (lowest calibration cross y = -74.9 mm in notebooks/week-03/Choton/code/config/homography.json, minus the 20 mm margin of yolo_lib._belt_zone). Run testing/live_runs/20261117_190902.csv with the line at -60 mm: the belt moved the candies about 130 mm in 1.2 s (about 100 mm/s), and the candy that stopped it came to rest at y = -93.3 mm, 33 mm past the line and 1.6 mm inside the pick area. At -30 mm an item rests at about -63 mm, about 30 mm inside the pick area Moved from -30 to -15 on 17 Nov after testing/live_runs/20261117_220813.csv: the belt moves about 120 mm/s, and items stopped for at y = -56 and -80 mm came to rest at -94.8 and -113.7 mm, at and beyond the end of the pick area (-94.9 mm). The late stops came from slow pictures (0.2 to 0.35 s each, since fixed in vision_session.py); -15 leaves room if a picture is slow again

feed_stop_line_frames.unit: pictures in a row with a needed object at the stop line before the belt stops
feed_stop_line_frames.source: chosen: one wrong detection does not stop the belt; at 10 frames/s the second picture adds 0.1 s (about 3 mm of belt travel)

refeeds_without_pick_max.unit: times in a row the object belt runs again when the pictures hold none of the objects the box still needs; then PAUSED (object missing)
refeeds_without_pick_max.source: chosen: the rest of the set may still be on the belt, but a wrong detection must not keep starting the belt

gone_match_px.unit: px: an object this close to a picked one counts as already picked

box_leave_timeout_s.unit: s for the closed box to leave the robot

close_lid.unit: true = put the lid on every box
close_lid.source: notebooks/week-03/Choton/Choton_Week3_Notebook.md 14 Nov (closing the box); lid heights still missing in settings.json (CONFIRM)

move_reply_timeout_s.unit: s: longest wait for one robot reply (a Sync waits for the queued moves); longer = FAULT
move_reply_timeout_s.source: chosen for real runs: a reply that never comes must stop the run instead of letting it continue

camera_frame_max_age_s.unit: s: newest camera frame must be younger than this to arm
camera_frame_max_age_s.source: chosen for real runs: an older frame shows the cell as it was, not as it is

arm_token_s.unit: s an arm token stays valid
arm_token_s.source: chosen for real runs: Start must follow Arm closely

box_restart.unit: how the closed box moves on: dobot_output (pulse dobot.box_belt_do), nano_auto (the box belt controller does it; we watch), operator (a person takes it; we watch)
box_restart.source: team decision 17 Nov (team decision 17 Nov): a person takes the closed box off; the UNO then brings the next box to the sensor

object_belt_serial.unit: serial number of the object belt (Dobot Mini Conveyor Belt DT-AC-CB070-02E): cards and candies
object_belt_serial.source: label, read by the team on 17 Nov (17 Nov)

box_belt_serial.unit: serial number of the box belt (Dobot Mini Conveyor Belt DT-AC-CB070-02E): boxes and lids
box_belt_serial.source: photos of the station, 17 Nov: photo 8 (label readable)

index.unit: OpenCV camera index on this laptop

fps_sample_frames.unit: frames grabbed to measure frames per second

poll_interval_s.unit: s between model checks (loading is slow)

live_detect_interval_s.unit: s between live detections for the Vision screen (only while no run is active)
live_detect_interval_s.source: chosen for the console: enough for the screen, light on the laptop CPU

top_edge_objects_usable.unit: true/false: a card or candy that touches only the TOP border of the camera picture (the robot side of the object belt) is counted and picked, with the centre of what the camera sees; false = Choton's rule, every object at a picture border is ignored
top_edge_objects_usable.source: false since the camera was re-aimed on 17 Nov (calibration of 2026-11-17_21-26-54): the object belt with its robot-side rail is now inside the picture (rail at about v = 50 px), so an item on the belt no longer touches the top border, and what does touch it comes from outside the picture (17 Nov 21:50: the robot arm standing in the picture was seen as card 0.88 at the top border and counted). Was true with the camera view of 14:30, where the top border ran along that rail and four cards in a row rode through the pick area marked AT THE EDGE (testing/live_runs/20261117_195652.csv); set it to true again only if the camera is aimed like that again

bottom_edge_box_and_lid_usable.unit: true/false: a box or a lid that touches only the BOTTOM border of the camera picture is used (the box as it is seen; the lid with the centre of the whole lid worked out from vision.lid_apparent_size_mm); false = Choton's rule, every object at a picture border is ignored
bottom_edge_box_and_lid_usable.source: chosen 17 Nov after the camera was re-aimed (calibration notebooks/week-03/Choton/code/config/homography.json of 2026-11-17_21-26-54): the picture's bottom border is at robot x 408 to 423 mm, and the far wall of a box standing across the box belt at the box slot (349.6, 38.7) appears at about 430 mm, so the box and a lid lying beside it are cut by about 10 to 15 mm

lid_apparent_size_mm.unit: mm [long side, short side] of the lid's outline as the camera measures it on the belt calibration (the lid's top is about 24 mm above the belt, so this is a little more than its real size); used to work out the centre of a lid that the bottom border cuts; null = such a lid is not taken
lid_apparent_size_mm.source: outline of the whole lid (Choton's object_angle: GrabCut + minAreaRect) in three pictures of 17 Nov with the 14:30 calibration (2.39 px/mm across the belts, 2.375 px/mm along them): testing/live_runs/20261117_204758_pictures/0007_look.jpg 387 x 283 px = 161.8 x 119.2 mm; testing/calibration_backup/lid_whole_2026-11-17_1858.jpg 372 x 285 px = 156.6 x 119.1 mm; testing/calibration_backup/lid_whole_2026-11-17_1830.jpg 371 x 298 px = 156.2 x 124.6 mm. Spread about 4 mm, so the worked-out centre is good to about 2 to 3 mm

stream_max_fps.unit: frames per second, highest rate of the camera stream to the browser
stream_max_fps.source: chosen for the console: a frame rate limit keeps the laptop CPU free

valid_from.unit: date of the current worktable and camera stand: a homography.json made before it is refused
valid_from.source: Choton's handover, lab 17 Nov (new worktable and camera stand, 15_robot_setup.py): new worktable and camera stand; the calibration must be done again if the camera or the robot moves

value.why: the camera turned 6.3 deg in its holder between 21:50 and 21:58 on 17 Nov

view_correction.unit: 3 x 3 matrix: pixel in the camera view of today -> pixel in the view the calibration was made in; used only with the calibration whose created stamp is for_calibration; null = the calibration is used as it is
view_correction.source: worked out from two console pictures of 17 Nov, testing/calibration_backup/view_2026-11-17_2150_as_calibrated.jpg and view_2026-11-17_2158_after_the_camera_turned.jpg: 479 picture features of the table, rails and labels moved together (turned -6.29 deg, scale 0.999, mean residual 0.87 px), and the two calibration crosses still in view (marks 1 and 4, one on each belt) are found within 0.3 px of where this matrix puts them. Not a new calibration: the robot did not touch the marks again

board.unit: box belt controller board: runs the box belt on the E18-D80NK sensor and sends the step pulses of both belt drivers
board.source: photos of the station, 17 Nov: photo 7; notebooks/week-03/Rashmika/Readme.md sections 2.3 and 2.5; sketch notebooks/week-03/Rashmika/ArduinoCode/ArduinoCode.ino

serial_port.unit: serial port of the box belt controller on this PC, e.g. COM5 (Windows Device Manager)
serial_port.source: not used: the sketch (notebooks/week-03/Rashmika/ArduinoCode/ArduinoCode.ino) sends nothing over USB, and the UNO runs on a USB-C supply, not connected to this PC

baud.source: not used: the sketch (notebooks/week-03/Rashmika/ArduinoCode/ArduinoCode.ino) sends nothing over USB, and the UNO runs on a USB-C supply, not connected to this PC

status_command.unit: text the box belt controller answers with its sensor and belt state
status_command.source: not used: the sketch (notebooks/week-03/Rashmika/ArduinoCode/ArduinoCode.ino) sends nothing over USB, and the UNO runs on a USB-C supply, not connected to this PC

sensor_active_level.unit: 0 or 1 at the sensor input when a box is there
sensor_active_level.source: sketch notebooks/week-03/Rashmika/ArduinoCode/ArduinoCode.ino: pin 5 with INPUT_PULLUP; LOW for 50 ms = a box is seen, the box belt's ENA (pin 6) goes LOW and the belt stops. The E18-D80NK is NPN: LOW when it sees an object

poll_interval_s.unit: s between box belt controller checks

folder.unit: folder with Choton's code on this computer
folder.source: repo path, exists on this PC (checked 2026-11-16); change it if his code lives elsewhere

host.source: chosen: the API is not exposed to the network
